basis: Nephrotic syndrome 4/5, proteinuria 20/20; cardiac failure 11/13 and cytopenias are core. Frequent skeletal, CNS and optic damage omitted by four-axis cap.
Defined by high-flow vascular malformations, persistent cutaneous capillary malformations and bony/soft-tissue limb overgrowth.
Mitochondrial metabolic disease defined by cerebellar ataxia and sensory neuropathy; ophthalmoplegia does not establish intrinsic eye damage. Thyroiditis is separate.
Umbrella for inherited ocular developmental disorders; skeletal involvement belongs to particular subtypes.
Embryonal malignancy arising in the brain or spinal cord.
Defined by congenital absence of substantial portions of the brain and overlying skull.
Hyperplasia originates in the adrenal medulla, an endocrine organ.
Tumor originates in the fallopian tube, outside the axes; reproductive smooth muscle is not skeletal muscle. EBV association is not established for this concept.
Hereditary motor tract disease causing spastic paraplegia; muscle spasms reflect neurologic dysfunction rather than primary muscle damage.
Direct infectious arthritis and meningitis/cranial palsy are each annotated frequent (30-79%). Transient erythema and minority cardiac/ocular complications excluded.
Autoimmune blistering skin disease; oral mucosal blisters and stomatitis are frequent (30-79%), establishing direct oral damage.
Neonatal physiological withdrawal is defined by CNS hyperexcitability and neurobehavioral dysfunction; associated gastrointestinal signs do not establish organ damage.
Loss of atrial electrical and mechanical function; muscular dystrophy is a separate associated underlying disease, not damage caused by atrial standstill.
Umbrella for congenital joint contracture and limb malformation syndromes; neurologic causes are not shared across most subtypes.
Corpus callosum agenesis establishes CNS involvement; unspecified facial clefting provides insufficient detail to assign oral, skeletal or skin involvement.
Inherited dental enamel hypoplasia; teeth belong to the gastrointestinal axis.
Acute lymphoblastic blood/marrow malignancy with explicit lymphoma features; lymphoma warrants the infectious_immune mechanism axis.
Tyrosine catabolic defect with defining liver injury and renal tubulopathy; porphyria-like neuropathic crises affect roughly 40% untreated. Rickets is less frequent.
Congenital aortic arch diverticulum; usually asymptomatic. Airway/esophageal compression is not established as common direct organ damage; dissection is a risk.
Hereditary colorectal cancer syndrome; extracolonic malignancies are separate diseases whose risk is increased, not direct multisystem damage.
Congenital structural defect of the atrial or ventricular cardiac septum.
Defined malformations affect the inner ear semicircular canal and external/middle ear.
Mitochondrial myopathy with encephalopathy; hypertrophic cardiomyopathy in 1/2 annotated patients supports cardiac involvement, with small-sample uncertainty. Apnea may be central.
Subaortic fibrous obstruction directly restricts left ventricular outflow.
IgG4-mediated infiltration defines lacrimal and salivary gland disease. Other organ lesions are uncommon or separately diagnosed; tubulointerstitial nephritis is 1-4%.
